newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand issues positive key economic data.
newsitem.headline: Thailand issues positive key economic data.

text.p: The Thai finance ministry on Wednesday released key economic indicators showing narrower monthly trade and current account deficits in December.

Figures obtained from the ministry said the December trade deficit fell to 22.3 billion baht from 24.2 billion in November while the current account deficit declined to 19.1 billion baht from 21.7 billion.
The ministry said Thailand's trade deficit for the whole of 1996 stood at 417.6 billion baht against 434.0 billion estimated earlier by the central bank and an actual 373.8 billion in 1995.

It also revised the 1996 current account deficit to 372.6 billion baht from 384.0 billion seen previously by the Bank of Thailand. The current account deficit was 337.6 billion baht in 1995. Market analysts had viewed the current account deficit as a factor that could destabilise the country's short-term economic outlook.
Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan said the 1996 current account deficit amounted to 8.0 percent of gross domestic product, against 8.2 percent estimated earlier for the year and 8.1 percent in 1995.
The minister announced the figure after reviewing the 1996 economic performance with central bank officials.
The ministry said exports contracted 0.2 percent in 1996, little changed from a 0.1 percent decline expected earlier by the central bank for the year and against 23.6 percent growth in 1995.
It said import growth also slowed to only 2.3 percent in 1996 against the central bank's earlier 3.3 percent estimate for the year and an actual 30.5 percent increase in 1995.

The ministry also said foreign reserves looked healthier in January when it stood at $39.2 billion which amounted to 6.7 months of imports after they declined for two straight months and against $38.7 billion at end-December.
It said M-2 money supply also showed a positive slower growth trend in January when it rose about 10.9 percent year-on- year against a revised 12.9 percent in December.
The Bank of Thailand has strived to curb domestic money supply as part of its fight against inflation.
